dev_notes: src/commands/read.mjs. Together they are a couple of thousand tokens instead of the whole corpus, which is why an agent is told to read through them rather than opening the corpus.

history.name: Listing and reading entries
history.description: The command ledger list prints the whole corpus, one short line per feature: its size, its id, its name, and whether it is new or changed in the release in progress. It filters by area, audience, size, or by what has moved this cycle. The command ledger show prints the single entry you are about to edit, and prints every version it has been through when you ask for its history.

The command ledger list prints the corpus one line per feature, filtered by area, audience, size or what moved. The command ledger show prints one entry, its recorded changes, and on request its history or the last edition's text beside today's.
history.how_to_see: Run ledger show --diff with the id of an entry that changed in this release: it prints the last edition's text, today's text, and the changes recorded in between.

events.what: ledger show prints an entry's code and recorded changes, the entry as it stood at any version with --at, and with --diff, the last edition's text beside the current one.
events.why: That is what a person or an agent needs in front of them before saying what changed.

events.what: ledger show prints how to see the entry instead of the code it lives in.
events.why: The ledger no longer maps code to entries.
